thread:
leah-sales: Heads up team — ArcusBank wants a final POC runbook and cost breakdown for an enterprise commit. Traffic profile: target 200 RPS sustained, median gen ~300 tokens, spikes up to 420 RPS for short bursts, occasional 3k-token long contexts. They want reserved GPUs for baseline and an autoscale fallback. Can we bullet a simple runnable plan + billing option?

tom-eng: Quick clarifying Qs: which model and quantization are they using in tests? And are they okay with adaptive truncation for long contexts?

leah-sales: They tested a 34B quantized model (q5_1), context cap 4k in their sandbox. They're open to truncation if we recommend it.

evan-ml: For 34B q5_1 our measured median throughput is ~30 RPS per Ampere GPU for 300-token median, long contexts drop throughput heavily — roughly 0.25x at 3k tokens. So baseline math: 200 RPS / 30 -> ~6.7 GPUs => round up to 7 reserved GPUs to hit sustained.

mike-sre: I'd propose reserve 7 GPUs in two AZs (4 + 3) for baseline. Autoscale pool up to +4 GPUs for bursts to 420 RPS (7 baseline *30 =210 RPS; add 4 *30 =120 => 330, that still short of 420 because long contexts reduce throughput). We should model worst-case and include fallback model routing to a 13B quantized variant for overloads.

ravi-platform: Alternative hybrid: reserve 6 GPUs (saves cost) + guaranteed burst bucket of 4 GPUs via burst credits and a policy to route >350 RPS to smaller model. Pricing option A: fixed monthly reserved fee for 6 GPUs + burst-cap credits (prepaid X hours) billed at reduced burst rate. Pricing option B: 7 reserved with smaller burst bucket. I'll produce both tables.

clare-legal: They're asking for an infra diagram, explicit statement that transient tensors never written to persistent storage, KMS control for any model keys, and data residency statement (EU region). Also want agreement language for preheat time (we should specify expected warmup <15m for usual prompts) and eviction fallback commitments.

mike-sre: Runbook outline (short):
- baseline: 6 reserved GPUs in 2 AZs (3+3)
- burst: autoscale group capped at 10 GPUs total, burst credits apply
- warmup: KV prefix replay for top N prompts + kernel cache priming
- canary: route 1% traffic to new pool, validate p95 latency and token/sec
- fallback: route to 13B-q model if queue depth > 50 or p95 > SLA
- oncall: arcus_poc_oncall@redwood with 60m response for capacity incidents (first 48h of ramp)

leah-sales: Can you paste example warmup and autoscale snippets? Client wants runnable steps.

evan-ml: Warmup example (shell):

```
# warmup_prompts.sh
while read -r p; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d "{\"model\":\"34b-q\",\"input\":\"$p\",\"max_tokens\":10}" >/dev/null
done < top_prompts.txt
```

mike-sre: Autoscale policy (conceptual YAML):

```
autoscale:
  min_replicas: 6
  max_replicas: 10
  cpu_threshold: 75%
  gpu_util_threshold: 68%
  scale_step: 1
  cooldown: 60s
  long_context_adjustment: true
  fallback_route: model:13b-q
```

ravi-platform: Canary checklist (short):
- deploy 1 warm worker in AZ-B
- run warmup script top_prompts.txt (5x)
- confirm p95 latency <= 1.8s and token/sec within 90% of baseline
- promote to 5% traffic -> monitor 15m -> full rollout

clare-legal: For the questionnaire I can provide templated answers. Action item: sales attach completed questionnaire doc. I'll return marked DOCX within 24h.

mike-sre: Oncall play (capacity spike):
1) alert triggers: queue_depth>40 or p95>3s
2) runbook step: add 1 burst GPU via autoscale -> wait 90s -> if unhealthy roll traffic to 13B-q pool -> notify arcus_poc_oncall -> open incident channel.

leah-sales: Billing detail convo; Arcus wants predictable monthly cost but 1) wants burst headroom and 2) needs to understand burn rate if they exceed burst credits. Let's be explicit in docs.

ravi-platform: I'll provide a cost table showing monthly reserved cost (6 GPUs) vs incremental per-hour burst cost and an example worst-case burn scenario (100% burst for 2h/day -> estimated monthly overage). Also include a chart mapping tokens/sec to GPU-hours.

tom-eng: Technical note: enforce request-side token caps (e.g., max_gen_tokens=2048) and use adaptive truncation heuristics server-side to avoid OOMs on long contexts. Also recommend session-level KV caching TTL=12h for POC.

leah-sales: Timeline? They want this package tomorrow midday. Who's owning final doc?

ravi-platform: I'll own collating runbook + pricing tables. Evan will add warmup prompts and perf notes. Mike adds oncall and canary steps. Clare will provide legal templates. I'll publish a shared doc and ping once ready.

deploy-bot: Shared doc created: ArcusBank_POC_Runbook_v2 at https://docs.redwood.example/ArcusBank_POC_Runbook_v2 (editors: #sales #eng #sre #legal).

leah-sales: Awesome — I'll send to Arcus infra once you drop the draft. Thanks all :raised_hands:
